call_chain.finding: The case drops stdout_rx, directly awaits timeout(2 seconds, exit_rx), and retains the session. It does not call the changed output collector.

The empty inherited-FD list selects portable. Unix uses the common PtyIo AsyncFd reader, not portable-pty blocking reader. The child is spawned before the reader/writer tasks. Portable child wait runs in spawn_blocking.

The duplicated master descriptor shares O_NONBLOCK. The reader continues after channel send failure. EOF and non-Interrupted read errors end the reader silently, so existing evidence cannot tell why or whether it ended.

The session retains writer_tx, so dropping the output receiver does not close input or send VEOF. has_exited/exit_code are waiter-published observations, not an independent OS process liveness query. terminate happens only after timeout in this case.

The Python -c script records startup, performs a single 4 MiB buffered write of x bytes, then updates the side-channel file. It is noninteractive; the previous PyREPL probe backlog is not this execution path. The last visible marker does not identify the blocked syscall or bytes drained.
At the inspected fixed Tokio tag, async_io clears readiness only for actual WouldBlock; success returns without clearing. The product closure reads the real descriptor and uses only READABLE.
The inspected fixed Mio tag registers read and write filters separately with EV_CLEAR. No unsupported combined interest or synthetic WouldBlock is introduced by the product source.
